To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the job resources of rewards/ recognition, job control and feedback were positively associated with job satisfaction, turnover intention, and the exhaustion component of mental health personnel burnout.
Job demands and job resources are related to burnout, turnover intent and job satisfaction.
Job demands and job resources are associated with burnout and turnover intentions in mental health personnel in one Australian mental health setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the job demands and job resource factors that are associated with burnout and turnover intentions in mental health personnel.
the development of a framework that will enable the identification of the key job demands and resources in mental health services and their relationship to burnout, turnover and job satisfaction.
the relationships between burnouts, turnover intention, and job satisfaction in mental health personnel in the context of job demands and resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
job resources and job demands are important in relation to burnout and turnover in the mental health sector.

mental health personnel who have high levels of burnout are likely to have low levels of job satisfaction, high levels of turnover intention and experience high levels of job demands, and low levels of job resources.
the Job Demands Resource model provides a useful framework for understanding the relationships between burnouts, turnover intention and the workplace environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
job resources are associated with lower burnout, lower turnover intention and higher job satisfaction.
job satisfaction, job resources and job demands are associated with turnover intention and burnouts.

the Job Demand Resources model provides a useful foundation for understanding the relationship between job demands and resources and the experience of burnout, job satisfaction and turnover intentions in this mental health service.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mental health services need to focus on job resources such as rewards and recognition, participation, and feedback in order to enhance job satisfaction, decrease turnover intention and reduce burnout.

mental health services need to ensure that they are supporting their staff with adequate job resources to enable them to perform their work effectively and to avoid burnout and the negative outcomes associated with it.
job resources are associated with burnout and job satisfaction, while job demands are associated with burn out.
